This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12%
p.a.
2.

The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 20.08.2023 at about 3.00 to 3.05 a.m. Disha Sharma was travelling as pillion rider on TVS Jupiter Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EF-2446 being rode by its rider by name Jose Bery near Saneshwara Temple, Lakshmipura, Kengeri Hobali,
Neeraj Sharma vs Geethika Sharma on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14023875/
2 Bengaluru South, Bengaluru at very high speed in rash and negligent manner, due to the said impact, motor cycle got toppled and both rider and Disha Sharma fell SCCH 5 down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, Disha Sharma was shifted to Astra Hospital and took treatment wherein Disha Sharma succumbed to fatal injuries on 22.08.2023 at about 5.15 p.m. Thereafter dead body was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, wherein post mortem examination was conducted and handed over dead body to petitioner, who performed funeral and obsequies ceremony by incurring Rs.4,00,000/-.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Disha Sharma was aged about 19 years, hale and healthy, she was studying BBA 3rd Sem., at Christ College, Bengaluru, she was very brilliant and distinction student in the college and had very bright future and prospective in her future and she was selected in IT Company at campus selection in the college, wherein salary also fixed at Rs.4,90,000/- p.a.
Due to untimely death of the deceased SCCH 5 in the tragic accident, petitioner has put to great financial hardship and untold misery and depressed.
With regard to accident, crime No.316/2023 is registered against the rider of the TVS Jupiter Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EF-2446 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner, respondent No.2 is insurer and respondent No.3 is rider of the said offending vehicle, they are liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the court through counsel and filed written statement and denies the issuance of insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EF-2446 and rider of the vehicle has no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
SCCH 5 Respondent No.2 seeks protection under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.1 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.159 of M.V.Act.
Further denied involvement of said offending vehicle in the alleged accident and further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive exorbitant.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.3 being rider of the TVS Jupiter motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EF-2446 appeared through counsel before the tribunal and filed written statement.

Respondent No.3 submitted that, deceased Disha Sharma had come with him and his friends to Burnout Cafe at Kanakapura Road on 20.08.2023 and also submitted that, he has rode the said offending vehicle on the date of accident.
Further submitted that, respondent No.1 is owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said vehicle and SCCH 5 insurance was valid as on the date of accident.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6.

1. Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Disha Sharma died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.08.2023 at about 3.00 to 3.05 a.m. when deceased was travelling on a TVS Jupiter motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EF-2446 near Shaneshwara Temple, Lakshmipura Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru at that time, the rider of the said vehicle drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
SCCH 5 7.
In order to prove their case, Petitioner/ father of the deceased examined as PW-1 and exhibited 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
On the other hand, respondent No.3 has deposed his evidence as RW-1 and closed evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner/father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.

In this regard SCCH 5 he has exhibited copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest report as Ex.P.6, copy of P.M.Report as Ex.P.7, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.8.
10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those were marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 20.08.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, respondent No.3 being the rider of the TVS Jupiter motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-EF- 2446 is examined as RW-1.
R.W-1 stated thatat the time of accident he had valid driving licence and same was seized by Kanakapura police.

On perusal of Ex.P.8 chargesheet it was filed against the respondent No.3 for the offence punishable under section 279, 304A of IPC SCCH 5 and as per chargesheet there is no mention of violation of provision of M.V Act.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, it is proved by the PW-1 about death of Disha Sharma due to accident occurred on Neeraj Sharma vs Geethika Sharma on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14023875/
4 20.08.2023 at about 3.00 a.m. to 3.05 a.m. when she was proceeding as a pillion rider on TVS Jupiter Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53- EF-2446 near Saneshwara Temple, Lakshmipura,
Kengeri Hobali, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru.
12.
On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of the rider of the TVS Jupiter Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-EF-2446.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 13. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioner, deceased/Disha Sharma was aged about 19 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, petitioner has produced copy of Voter ID Card of the deceased as Ex.P.12, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 13.07.2004 and the alleged accident was occurred on 20.08.2023.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.12, age of the deceased is considered about 19 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

In this regard, petitioner has exhibited copy of study certificate as Ex.P.13, Christ college receipts as Ex.P.14, Christ college marks cards as Ex.P.15.

By considering the educational qualification which is undisputed fact this Tribunal is of a considered view that deceased Disha Sharma is potential to earn at least Rs.25,000/- and notional income is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.
15. Further petitioner No.1 is father of the deceased.
To prove the said fact, PW-1 has produced copy of aadhar card of petitioner which is marked as Ex.P.11, it reveals that, petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased Disha Sharma.

16. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased was bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so SCCH 5 that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.
